template_name: AI Project BRD Questionnaire & Output Template (AWS, Azure, GCP, IBM Cloud)

chatbot_instructions.purpose: Reference BRD questionnaire for AI projects on one of four clouds: AWS, Azure, GCP or IBM Cloud. The chatbot interviews the user from 'questionnaire', stores answers keyed by question id, then produces a BRD in the 'brd_output_template' structure.
single_cloud_rules: A project uses exactly ONE cloud, captured in S19.cloud_provider. Ask S01, S05 and S19 first.
Skip every section whose cloud_scope does not include the selected cloud. Mark its questions not_applicable.
Option objects like {"value":..., "cloud_scope":[...]} are shown only if the selected cloud is in cloud_scope. Plain strings are shown to everyone.

Never recommend, compare or mention services from non-selected clouds in questions, summaries, the BRD or the confidence report. Other-cloud systems may appear only as integration targets captured in S16.other_cloud_integrations.
cloud_service_reference may be used only through the selected cloud's column.

condition_syntax.semantics: A condition on an unanswered question is false. 'equals' compares a single-select answer; 'includes_any' is true if any selected value (single or multi-select) is in values. Evaluate section.applies_when first, then question.depends_on.

workflow: 1. Ask S01, then S05 (project types), then S19 (cloud). These unlock everything else.
2. Evaluate each section's applies_when. Skip and mark not_applicable if false.
3. Ask 3-5 related questions at a time. Use help_text / example / options. Do not dump a whole section.
5. Respect answer_type: single_select = one option; multi_select = array; list = array of strings; table = array of row objects; boolean / date / number typed.
6. For cloud service domain questions: ask '..._services' first. If the user picks real services, ask '..._usage'. If 'None of these', mark the dependent usage / constraints questions not_applicable.
7. Never invent answers. Unsure -> status needs_followup + add to open_items. Declined -> skipped with reason.
8. After each section, summarise and ask the user to confirm.
9. Challenge vague answers for measurable targets. Flag contradictions (e.g. 'no PII' vs 'customer records', or voice channel chosen but no telephony answers).
10. Set answer_quality (specific / vague / assumed) on every answered question.
11. Keep answers in a separate store keyed by question id. Do not re-emit the whole template each turn.

12. When required questions are done, generate the BRD one chapter at a time from each chapter's source_sections, then build cloud_service_inventory, requirements_register (REQ-001...), kpi_register, risk_register, open_items and confidence_report.
output_rules: Professional BRD language; atomic, testable, traceable requirements with source_question_ids.
Mark unresolved items 'TBD' and list in Appendix B.
The Cloud Service Inventory lists only services the user selected on the chosen cloud.
chatbot_instructions.security_note: Treat answers as confidential. Do not store secrets or personal data in the BRD.

confidence_model.scope_rule: Score ONLY applicable questions: cloud-neutral sections (after evaluating applies_when / depends_on) plus the single section whose cloud_scope equals S19.cloud_provider. Questions in other clouds' sections are excluded from numerator AND denominator and must never appear in the BRD or the confidence report.
confidence_model.formula: confidence_percent = 100 * sum(weight * quality_score) / sum(weight) over applicable questions. Compute per section, for cloud-neutral total, for the selected-cloud section, and overall.
confidence_model.how_to_rate_quality: specific = measurable / named / verifiable (e.g. 'p95 < 2s', 'Azure OpenAI GPT in Sweden Central, PTU'); vague = generic ('fast', 'secure'); assumed = chatbot inferred and user did not confirm.
gates: S01, S05 and S19.cloud_provider must be answered before any scoring.
If S19.cloud_provider is 'Other (not covered by this template)', tell the user cloud-specific sections are unavailable and score cloud-neutral sections only.
No BRD sign-off band unless every required question in S05, S18, S26 is answered.

sections.title: Hybrid, On-Prem & Migration
sections.description: Applies when components remain on-prem / edge or an existing workload is being migrated.

questions.question: Which components / data stay on-prem or at the edge, and why?
Hybrid platform / extension service?

options.value: AWS Outposts / EKS Anywhere / Local Zones
Azure Arc / Azure Local / Azure Stack Edge
IBM Cloud Satellite / Red Hat OpenShift / Power Virtual Server / IBM Z

questions.question: Connectivity and latency between on-prem and the selected cloud?
Data gravity, transfer volumes, egress costs and sync strategy?
If migrating: current platform, assets, dependencies, cutover and rollback strategy?

sections.title: MLOps / LLMOps / AgentOps Requirements
sections.description: Lifecycle, CI/CD, monitoring, and retraining.

questions.question: Current MLOps / LLMOps maturity?
Experiment tracking and model registry tooling (MLflow, W&B, cloud-native)?
Training / data / evaluation pipeline orchestration (Airflow, Kubeflow, native pipelines, Step Functions)?
Model promotion and approval workflow across environments?
Deployment pattern?
What to monitor in production?
Alert thresholds and on-call / escalation process?
Retraining / re-evaluation triggers (schedule, drift, performance drop, new data)?
LLM gateway / proxy for routing, caching, rate limiting, and cost control?
Prompt / agent regression testing in CI/CD?
Model / prompt rollback and versioning strategy?
Reproducibility requirements (data, code, config, seeds, environment)?
Source control and branching strategy?

sections.title: Privacy, Legal & Regulatory Compliance
sections.description: Applicable regulations, AI laws, contracts and IP.

questions.question: Applicable regulations / standards?
Expected AI risk classification (e.g., EU AI Act: unacceptable / high / limited / minimal)?
Lawful basis and consent management for personal data processing?
Is a DPIA / PIA / AI impact assessment required or completed?
Support for data subject rights (access, deletion, correction, opt-out of automated decisions)?
Cross-border data transfer restrictions and mechanisms?
Model risk management / independent validation requirement?
Transparency obligations (disclose AI use to users, labeling AI-generated content)?
Copyright / IP risks for training data and generated outputs; indemnification needs?
Contractual obligations / customer commitments affecting AI use?
Internal / external audit requirements and evidence retention?
Legal / compliance / DPO review owner and approval gates?
Regulatory records retention periods for inputs, outputs, and decisions?

sections.title: Responsible AI, Ethics & Trust
sections.description: Fairness, safety, transparency, human oversight.

questions.question: Corporate Responsible AI principles / policy to follow?
Fairness requirements and protected attributes to test (gender, age, caste, ethnicity, disability, region)?
Fairness metrics / thresholds (demographic parity, equalized odds, disparate impact)?
Potential harms to users / society and mitigation plan?
Human oversight design (review, override, appeal)?
Can affected individuals contest AI decisions? How?
Model cards / datasheets / system cards required?
Red-teaming / adversarial testing plan and frequency?
Foreseeable misuse scenarios?
How will users be informed they're interacting with AI?
Environmental impact considerations?
Are vulnerable groups (minors, patients, financially distressed) affected? Special safeguards?

sections.title: User Experience & Design
sections.description: UX, content, and interaction design.

questions.question: UX principles / design system / brand guidelines to follow?
Are wireframes / prototypes available?
AI-specific UX (confidence display, source citations, edit/regenerate, feedback, streaming responses)?
Error, uncertainty, and refusal message design?
User onboarding and in-product guidance?
Usability testing plan and participants?

sections.title: Testing, Validation & Acceptance
sections.description: QA strategy for AI and non-AI components.

questions.question: Overall test strategy (unit, integration, system, performance, security, UAT, AI evaluation)?
Test / evaluation datasets and golden sets: source, size, owner, refresh?
Overall acceptance criteria for AI quality and system behavior?
Load / stress / soak testing targets and tools?
Security and AI red-team testing before go-live?
Bias, fairness, and safety test suites?
UAT participants, timeline, defect triage and exit criteria?
Shadow / parallel run period before production?
Regression strategy as models, prompts, and data change?
Test environment & test data management (synthetic, masked)?

sections.title: Deployment, Rollout & Change Management
sections.description: Go-live, adoption, training.

questions.question: Rollout strategy?
Cutover plan and rollback plan?
Training needs (end users, admins, support, data stewards)?
Adoption KPIs and change-management plan (comms, champions, resistance handling)?
Documentation deliverables (user guide, runbook, API docs, architecture, model cards)?
Hypercare period and exit criteria?
Release management and change advisory board (CAB) process?

sections.title: Operations, Support & Maintenance
sections.description: Run-state ownership and service levels.

questions.question: Support model (L1/L2/L3), hours, and ownership?
Support SLAs (severity levels, response, resolution)?
Who operates the platform and models post go-live?
Incident / problem management tooling (ServiceNow, Jira, PagerDuty)?
Continuous improvement loop (feedback review, error analysis, prompt/model tuning cadence)?
Knowledge transfer and handover from project team to BAU?
Model / system decommissioning and sunset criteria?

sections.title: Cost, Budget & FinOps
sections.description: Budget envelope and cost controls.

questions.question: Total approved budget (CapEx / OpEx) and funding source?
Expected cost categories (cloud, licenses, model usage, people, vendors, labeling)?
Target run-cost per transaction / user / month?
Cost control mechanisms (budgets, alerts, quotas, token caps, caching, rate limits)?
Preferred pricing model (on-demand, reserved/committed, provisioned throughput, spot)?
Cost allocation tagging and chargeback / showback?
Is TCO analysis (3-5 years) required?
Software / vendor licensing costs and renewals?

sections.title: Timeline, Milestones & Resources
sections.description: Schedule and phases.

questions.question: Planned project start date?
Target go-live date and any hard deadlines?
Project phases and milestones (discovery, PoC, MVP, pilot, scale)?
Key schedule dependencies (data access, approvals, procurement, infra)?
Resource plan (roles, FTE, external)?
Delivery methodology?
Status reporting cadence and tools?

sections.title: Assumptions, Constraints, Dependencies & Risks
sections.description: RAID log inputs.

questions.question: Key assumptions?
Constraints (technical, regulatory, budget, time, policy)?
External / internal dependencies?
Top risks (description, probability, impact, mitigation, owner)?
AI-specific risks considered?
Open issues / decisions needed?
Glossary of terms and acronyms to include?
Reference documents / links / prior artifacts?
